stories.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
stories.body: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.

stories.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
stories.body: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.

stories.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
stories.body: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.

stories.title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
stories.body: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.

stories.title: When will we see Robert Pattinson as Bond in cinemas?
stories.body: Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, becoming the seventh actor to take up the mantle of 007.

stories.title: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
stories.body: Professor Michael Freeman tells BBC Newsnight that he believes the convicted sex offender's injuries are consistent with a homicide.

stories.title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children
stories.body: The 36-year-old's first trial this year fell apart when a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict.

stories.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
stories.body: The shootings in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng highlight South Africa's struggle to curb violent crime.

stories.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction
stories.body: The French film star was due to start an appeal trial after being found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a Paris set.

stories.title: Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations
stories.body: British singer Raye lands 11 nominations while Dolly Parton is recognised two months after her death.

stories.title: Ashes of exiled Nobel Laureate Miguel Ángel Asturias returned to Guatemala
stories.body: The poet, writer and diplomat died in Europe in 1974 having been forced to leave his native country.

stories.title: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
stories.body: The Estonian government says Russia was behind the attempted sabotage, which the Kremlin denies.

stories.title: Street cricket with a legend then metro ride as William and Kate begin India visit
stories.body: The Prince and Princess of Wales are visiting Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize this week, but started their trip with some fun outings.

stories.title: New York teen reunites with cat missing after building collapse
stories.body: Rescuers found the pet cat in the ruins of Zariah's apartment four days after she made an emotional plea to the public.

stories.title: Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip
stories.body: The Pope took to the skies before arriving in Cusco on the penultimate day of his Latin America tour.

stories.title: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
stories.body: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".

stories.title: Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin
stories.body: Some Russian tycoons are pining after a return to a 1990s system of oligarchy, when businessmen enjoyed power.

stories.title: Robert Pattinson: How the Twilight star became 007
stories.body: The Twilight, Batman and Odyssey star's profile will go even more stellar when he plays James Bond.

stories.title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?
stories.body: India has softened its recruitment scheme, giving young soldiers a longer military stint and another shot at permanent service.

stories.title: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?
stories.body: EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.
